title: Career Graph v1
description: A career expressed as timestamped entities with lifecycles, for rendering as an explorable city. The consumer of this contract does not know or care whose career it is: it reads dates and decides what exists, what is under construction, and what has been upgraded at any point on a timeline. Chronicle is one producer of this shape; any system that can emit it can drive the same renderer.

version.description: Contract major version. A consumer must refuse a version it does not understand rather than guess.

generatedAt.description: When this document was produced. Not when anything in it happened.

subject.description: Whose career this is. Presentation only - the renderer never branches on it.

entities.description: Everything in the city. Flat rather than nested, because an entity's place in the world is decided by its own dates and district, not by where it sits in a document.

id.description: Stable across regenerations. A consumer animating between two documents relies on this to know that a building moved rather than that one vanished and another appeared.

kind.description: What this becomes in the world. building = a capability that grows in place; road = work that connects capabilities; district = a grouping; landmark = a moment that happened once.

district.description: The id of the district this belongs to, or null for entities that stand alone.

built.description: When this came into existence. Before this date the renderer must not show it at all - that is the entire premise of the timeline.

upgraded.description: Dates on which this grew. A capability deepening is an upgrade in place, never a replacement, so a building gains storeys rather than being demolished and rebuilt.

retired.description: When this stopped being current, if it ever did. Not a deletion: the renderer may show it unlit or weathered rather than removing it, because it did happen.

magnitude.description: Relative size, 0 to 1, normalised by the producer. Height for a building, width for a road. Normalised rather than raw because only the producer knows what the maximum means - years of experience, lines of code, or something else entirely.

connects.description: For roads: the entity ids this links. A project connects the capabilities it used, which is what makes it visually obvious how the pieces worked together.

speculative.description: True for anything stated as an intention rather than a fact. The renderer MUST make these unmistakably different from built entities - blueprints, scaffolding, holograms. This flag is what lets the city be ambitious without being dishonest.

href.description: Where to read more, if anywhere. Absolute.

meta.description: Producer-specific extras. A consumer must ignore anything here it does not recognise, so a producer can add detail without breaking every renderer.
